title: The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036 (February 2026)

verified.claim: CBO projects consumer price inflation (CPI-U) of 2.8% in 2026, settling at 2.3% from 2028 onward.
verified.quote: It reaches 2.8 percent in 2026, returns to 2.3 percent (or about 0.3 percentage points above PCE inflation) in 2028, and remains at that level through the rest of the projection period.

verified.claim: CBO gives a two-thirds chance that the 10-year Treasury rate in 2026 lies between 3.5% and 4.8%: even one-year projections carry a wide range.
verified.quote: the interest rate on 10-year Treasury notes will be between 3.5 and 4.8 percent.

title: How Changes in Revenues and Outlays Would Affect Debt Service, Deficits, and Debt: 2026 to 2036 — Treasury yields table

verified.claim: CBO projects 10-year Treasury notes at 4.1% (2026) rising to 4.4% (2032-2036), and 3-month bills at 3.4% falling to 3.1%.

agency: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), republishing FHFA, BLS and Federal Reserve Board data
title: Annual series 1975-2025: FHFA house price indexes (San Jose metro, San Francisco metro division, California), CPI-U, San Francisco-area rent CPI, 3-month Treasury bill, 10-year Treasury
note: Second request for rates: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=CPIAUCNS,TB3MS,GS10&cosd=1975-01-01&coed=2025-12-31&fq=Annual,Annual,Annual&fam=avg,avg,avg . Values were transcribed by hand into data/official/fred_annual.csv and spot-checked; anyone can reproduce the table by opening the URL.

verified.claim: San Jose metro house prices rose from an index of 23.21 (end 1976) to 560.05 (end 2025), but fell from 114.25 (end 1989) to 99.95 (end 1994) and from 318.32 (end 2006) to 235.66 (end 2011).
Consumer prices (December CPI-U) rose from 58.2 in 1976 to 324.054 in 2025; one-year inflation ranged from about 0.1% (2008) to over 13% (1979).
3-month Treasury bills averaged 14.03% in 1981 and 0.03% in 2014.
